script:
export const meta = {
  name: 'restore-doc-rewrite',
  description: 'Draft a Mac-true ~/.claude/RESTORE.md into the scratchpad, then fact-check every path and command (read-only)',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Draft', detail: 'one writer, scratchpad only' },
    { title: 'Check', detail: 'verify each path/command on disk' },
  ],
}

const OUT = '/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/14b675be-8339-493c-8201-2773fa3f3381/scratchpad/RESTORE.draft.md'
const RULES = `
HARD RULES: Do not edit, move or delete anything outside ${OUT}. Never read or walk ~/Library/CloudStorage or ~/DEV/_DRIVE (Drive FUSE hangs). Never open DexaProject, Linda_Projects, SpecialRequests. Never print secret values: Keychain item NAMES only (e.g. from ~/.zshrc 'security find-generic-password -s NAME' lines), never values. No network. 'timeout' is not installed.`

phase('Draft')
const draft = await agent(
`Write a new Mac-true recovery guide for Eric Rash's agent setup and save it to ${OUT} (create the file with your Write tool). It will replace ~/.claude/RESTORE.md, which today gives Windows steps (robocopy from G:\\, Task Scheduler, Milvus, bare pip install) and is uploaded to Drive nightly by ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 (lines ~792-798), so it is the copy Eric would read on a phone during a real restore.

Read first: ~/.claude/RESTORE.md (keep what is still true), ~/.claude/START-HERE.md Part 2 (the exFAT-drive Mac restore runbook that was actually executed once — fold in its checkpoints that still apply), ~/.claude/MIGRATION-MACOS.md, ~/.claude/RECOVERY-INVENTORY.md, ~/.claude/STORAGE.md (the 'Machine-written copies (backups)' and 'Agent files' sections are current truth), ~/.claude/scripts/backup-manifest.json (destinations), ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 (which tgz files it uploads to Drive _MACHINE/Backups/Machine: grep for '.tgz'), ~/.claude/machine.md and ~/.claude/TOOLPATHS.md.

Required content, under 120 lines, plain imperative steps, Mac only:
1. What lives where: one short table, then point at ~/.claude/STORAGE.md.
2. Accounts needed first (GitHub erash11, Google, claude.ai) — no secrets.
3. Clone the config repos to their exact paths: dotclaude -> ~/.claude, claude-skills -> ~/.claude/skills, claude-global-memory -> ~/.claude/global-memory, claude-memory-compiler -> ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler, the DEV thin repo -> ~/DEV (its .gitignore starts with /* — never remove), then project repos via 'gh repo list erash11'. Verify each remote URL from the live clones (git -C <path> remote get-url origin).
4. Pull machine backups: FIRST route is the drive.google.com web UI -> _MACHINE/Backups/Machine (gws is not authorized on a fresh Mac); gws only after 'gws auth login'. List the real tgz names daily-backup uploads and what each restores to.
5. CRASHBOX SSD captures (what is there, from the manifest 'ssd' destination).
6. Secrets: from the macOS Keychain; list item NAMES only.
7. Tooling: Homebrew, uv at ~/.local/bin/uv (not Homebrew), never global pip (PEP 668), 'uv sync' for the memory compiler, the LaunchAgents restore (launchagents.tgz -> ~/Library/LaunchAgents, then launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) per plist), Full Disk Access for Terminal (cloud-push needs it).
8. The START-HERE corrections that still apply on the Mac.
9. 'Deliberately NOT backed up' (keep the current list if still true) and 'Keeping this document honest' (one short rule).
Delete both pointers to MIGRATION-MACOS.md. Use ASD-STE100-style plain English: short sentences, one instruction each. Return a list of every path and command you put in the doc, and anything you could not verify.
${RULES}`,
  { label: 'draft', phase: 'Draft', schema: { type: 'object', properties: {
      written: { type: 'boolean' }, lines: { type: 'number' },
      claims: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'every path, repo URL, tgz name, plist, keychain name and command in the doc' },
      unverified: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } }, required: ['written', 'claims'] } })

phase('Check')
const check = await agent(
`Fact-check the draft recovery guide at ${OUT} for Eric Rash's Mac. Read it in full. For every path, repo URL, tgz name, plist label, Keychain item name and command in it, verify against the live Mac: the path exists (or is correctly described as created by the step), the remote URL matches 'git -C <path> remote get-url origin', each tgz name is one daily-backup.ps1 really uploads (grep ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1), each plist exists in ~/Library/LaunchAgents, each Keychain name appears in ~/.zshrc or ~/.zshenv (do not read values), each command is valid on macOS zsh with BSD tools. Also check that nothing in it is Windows-only, that it is under 120 lines, that it never tells the reader to remove '/*' from ~/DEV/.gitignore or run 'memsearch index' by hand, and that it does not contain a secret value.
The drafter's own claim list: ${JSON.stringify(draft?.claims || [])}
Return each wrong or doubtful line with the exact correction text. Do NOT edit the file.
${RULES}`,
  { label: 'fact-check', phase: 'Check', schema: { type: 'object', properties: {
      problems: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: {
        line_text: { type: 'string' }, problem: { type: 'string' }, correction: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['line_text', 'problem', 'correction'] } },
      verified_count: { type: 'number' }, verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['ready', 'ready_after_fixes', 'not_ready'] } },
    required: ['problems', 'verdict'] } })

return { draft, check }

claims: FILE /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kristinarash-DEV/14b675be-8339-493c-8201-2773fa3f3381/scratchpad/RESTORE.draft.md (119 lines, 0 MIGRATION-MACOS.md pointers, all bash blocks pass bash -n)
Football thin repo with 16 nested repos; LibraryProject with 1 nested repo
CRASHBOX codex/ (no work/), gemini/, LaunchAgents/, SecondBrain/ (no .git), DEV-repo-data/<repo>/, DEV-working-tree/<repo>/, DEV-nonrepo/<folder>/, DexaProject/, _receipts/
codex-memories.tgz (source missing; can be old or absent)
Keychain item typesafe-api-key (read by ~/.zshenv into TYPESAFE_API_KEY)
Keychain item Claude Code-credentials (written by Claude Code at sign-in)
gh auth login && gh auth setup-git

npm install -g @googleworkspace/cli && gws auth login -s drive
gws drive files list --params "{\"q\":\"'1ALag3z9Ew5ihBZKjt_1yZzsNpX-K4UJn' in parents and trashed = false\",\"fields\":\"files(id,name,size,modifiedTime)\"}"
for d in daily knowledge reports; do rsync -a "$SSD/claude/claude-memory-compiler/$d/" ~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/$d/; done
brew install gh git go node powershell/tap/powershell ripgrep tmux rclone yt-dlp ocrmypdf poppler pipx r ghidra

for f in ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.keystone.*.plist; do [skip rituals]; launchctl bootstrap gui/$(id -u) "$f"; done
System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access > Terminal
clone repair: git init -b main; git remote add origin <url>; git fetch origin; git reset --mixed origin/main; git ls-files -z --deleted | xargs -0 git checkout --
unverified: Full Disk Access for Terminal: the task asked for this step, but my sources only show that FDA on Python.app and rsync did not help, and that the real fix is the Terminal launcher (cloud-push-launch.sh). I could not confirm that Terminal itself needs FDA. I did not read TCC.db.
gws on a fresh Mac: gws auth login needs ~/.config/gws/client_secret.json, and that file is in no backup. I did not test whether gws auth setup (needs gcloud) is the right fallback. No network.

I did not run the install URLs for uv (astral.sh/uv/install.sh) or Claude Code (claude.ai/install.sh), because there was no network. Only the resulting paths are confirmed: ~/.local/bin/uv, and ~/.local/bin/claude pointing to ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.310.

brew install --cask google-drive is not in this Mac's brew list --cask, so Drive was installed another way here. The cask name comes from START-HERE, not from this Mac. The brew formula list is copied from brew leaves. I left out the kitlangton-hex cask.

zotero.tgz: the stamp file ~/.claude/scripts/logs/zotero-snapshot.stamp is dated 2026-10-23 09:20. But no 'SNAP-GWS ... zotero.tgz : OK' line appears in the log, so the upload to Drive is not confirmed.
codex-memories.tgz: ~/.codex/memories is missing and every run logs 'SNAP skip (missing)'. I do not know whether an old copy is still on Drive.
CRASHBOX was not mounted. Its layout comes from daily-backup.ps1 and the STATE-SSD log lines of the 2026-10-22 run, not from a listing of the drive.

None of the restore commands were run on a fresh Mac. I tested only these in the scratchpad: the dotclaude init/fetch/checkout -f sequence, the clone-repair sequence, and bsdtar --strip-components 1. The gws list query quoting was not run.
memsearch config set embedding.provider onnx comes from START-HERE. The live ~/.memsearch/config.toml does show provider = "onnx", but I did not run the command.
I left out the memsearch 'flush patch' from START-HERE. No notes on it exist anywhere, and it may not apply to the uv-tool install (memsearch v0.4.17).

I could not check offline that dotclaude is a private repo. The old RESTORE.md says so. Note: dotclaude tracks 4,493 files under projects/ (session .jsonl transcripts and memory), so it holds session history that may contain secrets.
Repo counts (Football 16 nested, LibraryProject 1, skills near 65, 15 loaded com.keystone agents) are this Mac on 2026-10-24.

Manifest drift (I edited nothing): in backup-manifest.json, 18 DEV entries have remotes for folders that are no longer at ~/DEV/<name>. Examples are AgentAssist, morning-briefing and FootballWeightTargetTool. 34 top-level folders that are now git repos are still marked isRepo:false with no remote. Examples are Football, CLI_Dev, SpecialRequests and Baylor_Doc_Style. The backup still covers them, as non-repo SSD copies that include .git.

Not in any backup: ~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile, ~/.zshenv, ~/.gitconfig, ~/.claude.json (zotero MCP server), ~/.memsearch/config.toml and ~/.config/gws/client_secret.json. They are not in any repo or manifest path. The doc lists them as known gaps, but they are not fixed.

Possible side issue: in ~/.claude/scripts/setup-agents-symlinks.sh, the header says ~/.codex/AGENTS.md links to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md. The live link goes to ~/.claude/AGENTS.md. The doc uses the live target.

Disclosure: one find for nested .git folders under ~/DEV went into SpecialRequests directory names, because -mindepth 3 disabled the prune. It printed only counts. The manifest-drift loop also printed SpecialRequests' git origin URL. No file contents in SpecialRequests were read. DexaProject, Linda_Projects, ~/Library/CloudStorage and ~/DEV/_DRIVE were not opened or walked. readlink only.

Disclosure: I made and then removed a test folder of my own (scratchpad/gt) for the offline git and tar tests. Other scratchpad files were already there and I did not touch them. I printed Keychain and MCP names only, never values. I read only the mcpServers key names from ~/.claude.json.

problems.line_text: curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash            # claude -> ~/.local/bin/claude, NOT npm; then open a new terminal
problems.problem: The guide never says that ~/.claude/skill-router/ is in no repo and no backup. dotclaude's .gitignore '/*' ignores it, it is not its own repo, and the manifest has no entry for it. The UserPromptSubmit hook in ~/.claude/settings.json runs `python3 "$HOME/.claude/skill-router/router.py"` with no guard. Tested: python3 exits 2 when the file is missing, and a UserPromptSubmit hook that exits 2 blocks every prompt. So the first claude session on a restored Mac cannot take input. (The permission-gate and dcg hooks are guarded and only switch off.) The real fix is to track skill-router/ in dotclaude; until then the guide has to warn.
problems.correction: Keep the line. After the section 7 code block, add this bullet (and fold line 39 into line 38 so the file stays at 119 lines): "- Before the first `claude` start: `~/.claude/skill-router/` is in no repo and no backup, and the UserPromptSubmit hook in `~/.claude/settings.json` runs `skill-router/router.py` with no guard. If the file is missing, python3 exits 2 and Claude Code blocks every prompt. Copy the folder from the old Mac, or delete that hook entry until it is back."

problems.problem: On a fresh Mac this exits 2 and changes nothing. Script line 42 sets READY="$HOME/.agents/.sync-v2-ready" and refuses to run without it ('FATAL this machine is not prepared for the v2 sync'). No backup holds ~/.agents. The comment also leaves out the third view: the VIEWS array includes ~/.gemini/skills (added 2026-10-24, committed).
problems.correction: mkdir -p ~/.agents && touch ~/.agents/.sync-v2-ready && bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh   # fresh Mac: no old views to reconcile; rebuilds ~/.agents/skills, ~/.codex/skills, ~/.gemini/skills

problems.problem: `eval brew shellenv` only affects the current shell. The Homebrew installer does not write ~/.zprofile itself; it only prints the step. ~/.zprofile is in no backup (line 116). Line 85 then says to open a new terminal, and in that terminal /opt/homebrew/bin is off PATH. brew, gh, node/npm, go and pwsh all disappear, so line 92 (`go install`), line 105 (`pwsh ...`) and the node hooks in settings.json fail. On the live Mac, ~/.zprofile lines 4-8 hold the guarded shellenv block.

problems.line_text: tar -xzf codex-sessions.tgz -C ~/.codex; tar -xzf codex-agents.tgz -C ~/.codex; tar -xzf codex-sqlite.tgz -C ~/.codex
problems.problem: The live ~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1 no longer uploads codex-agents.tgz (or codex-memories.tgz). It now uploads codex-config.tgz, built by Snapshot-CodexConfig, whose root folder is codex-config/ with config.toml, hooks.json, rules, memories_1.sqlite, state_5.sqlite, history.jsonl and session_index.jsonl. Restoring that needs --strip-components 1. Caveat: this edit is uncommitted. The working copy grew from 825 to 987 lines during this check (saved 01:18) while HEAD bd5e08d still has the old lines, so re-grep the Snapshot-Gws lines once that edit is committed.
problems.correction: tar -xzf codex-sessions.tgz -C ~/.codex; tar -xzf codex-sqlite.tgz -C ~/.codex; tar -xzf codex-config.tgz --strip-components 1 -C ~/.codex   # config.toml, hooks.json, rules, history

problems.line_text: - Homebrew Python 3.14 is PEP 668-managed. Never `pip install` globally. Use a venv or `uv`. Go CLIs: `go install <module>@latest`, into `~/go/bin`. Each module path is in `~/.claude/skills/pp-*/SKILL.md`.
problems.problem: Only 2 pp-* skills exist (catapult, zotero), but ~/go/bin holds 8 binaries. `go version -m` gives the real module paths for the other six. The two zotero binaries are '(devel)' local builds from ~/DEV/CLI_Dev/printing-press/library/zotero-research-library (tracked in CLI_Dev, clean), not upstream @latest, and the `zotero` MCP in ~/.claude.json runs ~/go/bin/zotero-research-library-pp-mcp.
problems.correction: - Homebrew Python 3.14 is PEP 668-managed. Never `pip install` globally. Use a venv or `uv`. Go CLIs into `~/go/bin`: `go install github.com/mvanhorn/cli-printing-press/v4/cmd/cli-printing-press@latest`, and `go install github.com/mvanhorn/printing-press-library/library/<cat>/<name>/cmd/<name>-pp-cli@latest` for espn and movie-goat (media-and-entertainment), fireflies (productivity), flight-goat (travel), recipe-goat (food-and-dining). The zotero CLI and MCP are local builds: `cd ~/DEV/CLI_Dev/printing-press/library/zotero-research-library && go install ./cmd/...`.

problems.line_text: - Known gaps (in no backup; rebuild by hand): `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv` (brew shellenv, `~/.local/bin` and `~/go/bin` on PATH, the two Keychain exports), `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.claude.json` (the `zotero` MCP server), `~/.memsearch/config.toml`.
problems.problem: The list is incomplete. Neither the manifest nor daily-backup.ps1 covers ~/.agents/ (106 real third-party skill dirs plus .skill-lock.json, which names 45 installs). They also skip ~/.claude/skill-router/ and ~/.claude/permission-gate/ (both ignored by dotclaude) and ~/.claude/skills/.git/info/exclude (it hides 12 skill links; a clone does not carry it). The same goes for the ~/.local/bin tools besides uv/claude/memsearch/cli-hub: dcg, agy, herdr, ev, everythingd, ms-search, rea. Without dcg the PreToolUse guard hook switches off silently. ~/.zshrc also exports CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS and PFF_DB.
problems.correction: - Known gaps (in no backup; rebuild by hand): `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, `~/.zshenv` (brew shellenv, `~/.local/bin` and `~/go/bin` on PATH, the two Keychain exports, `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`, `PFF_DB`), `~/.gitconfig`, `~/.claude.json` (the `zotero` MCP server), `~/.memsearch/config.toml`, `~/.claude/skill-router/` and `~/.claude/permission-gate/`, `~/.agents/` (106 third-party skills and `.skill-lock.json`), `~/.claude/skills/.git/info/exclude`, and the `~/.local/bin` tools `dcg` (without it the guard hook switches off silently), `agy`, `herdr`, `ev`, `everythingd`, `ms-search`, `rea`.

problems.line_text: - Expect six `https://github.com/erash11/...` URLs, and `ls ~/.claude/skills | wc -l` near 65.
problems.problem: A fresh clone of claude-skills gives 48 top-level entries (git ls-tree HEAD without dotfiles). The live Mac shows 60, not 65. The extra 12 (anti-sleep, before-building, claudex-loop, claudex-route, cli-hub-meta-skill, codex-build, codex-review, decisions, design-taste-frontend, next-decision, persistent-localhost, scroll-craft) are symlinks into ~/.agents/skills, hidden from git by .git/info/exclude. No backup holds them. If they are reinstalled without that exclude file, the nightly Sync-Repo `git add -A` will commit them.
problems.correction: - Expect six `https://github.com/erash11/...` URLs, and `ls ~/.claude/skills | wc -l` = 48 right after the clone (the old Mac showed 60: the other 12 are links into `~/.agents/skills`, which no backup holds; add their names to `~/.claude/skills/.git/info/exclude` before reinstalling them, or the nightly backup commits them).

problems.line_text: - List project repos: `gh repo list erash11 --no-archived --limit 300`. Clone each into `~/DEV/<repo>`. `Website` clones from `erash11/AppliedPerformance-Site`.
problems.problem: 'Clone each' would also put the six config repos, AppliedPerformance-Site, the 16 Football nested repos and LibraryProject's nested repo into the top level of ~/DEV. daily-backup.ps1 is default-deny: any top-level ~/DEV folder that the manifest does not list adds 'manifest-unmanaged' and every run ends ERROR. Only Website differs from its repo name (checked across all ~/DEV folders); _ARCHIVE and docs are not repos.
problems.correction: - Clone each folder the area indexes (`~/DEV/FOOTBALL.md`, `PERFORMANCE.md`, `RESEARCH.md`, `PLATFORM.md`, `PROGRAM.md`, `PERSONAL.md`) name into `~/DEV/<folder>` from `erash11/<folder>`; `Website` clones from `erash11/AppliedPerformance-Site`. Use `gh repo list erash11 --no-archived --limit 300` only as a cross-check: an extra top-level folder in `~/DEV` makes every backup run end ERROR (`manifest-unmanaged`).

problems.problem: The guide restores ~/.gemini and gemini.tgz, builds ~/.gemini/skills and asks for a Gemini sign-in, but never installs the Gemini CLI. /opt/homebrew/bin/gemini is @google/gemini-cli@0.58.0 from npm. Other global npm packages on the live Mac: @playwright/cli, opencode-ai, @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent (Pi uses ~/.agents/skills), pptxgenjs, sharp.
problems.correction: npm install -g @openai/codex @googleworkspace/cli @google/gemini-cli   # also on the old Mac: @playwright/cli opencode-ai @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent pptxgenjs sharp

problems.line_text: - A plist that calls pwsh, git or uv directly needs an `EnvironmentVariables` PATH with `/opt/homebrew/bin`.
problems.problem: uv lives in ~/.local/bin, not /opt/homebrew/bin, so the PATH this line gives cannot find uv. Every live keystone plist that sets PATH uses /opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/Users/kristinarash/.local/bin:/Users/kristinarash/go/bin.
problems.correction: - A plist whose job calls pwsh, git, uv or a Go CLI needs an `EnvironmentVariables` PATH with `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/Users/<you>/.local/bin` (uv, claude) and `/Users/<you>/go/bin`, as the live plists have.

problems.line_text: - To repair a folder that already holds overlay files: `git init -b main`, `git remote add origin <url>`, `git fetch origin`, `git reset --mixed origin/main`, then `git ls-files -z --deleted | xargs -0 git checkout --`. This keeps the overlay edits.
problems.problem: Tested on a local bare repo: the recipe restores missing files and keeps the overlay edits, but leaves main with no upstream. `git pull` then fails with 'There is no tracking information for the current branch', which breaks the Session routine's git pull.
problems.correction: - To repair a folder that already holds overlay files: `git init -b main`, `git remote add origin <url>`, `git fetch origin`, `git reset --mixed origin/main`, `git branch -u origin/main`, then `git ls-files -z --deleted | xargs -0 git checkout --`. This keeps the overlay edits.

problems.line_text: - Copy a `DEV-nonrepo/<folder>` only when GitHub has no repo for it: its copy can hold an older `.git`. In each repo that took CRASHBOX files, run `git config core.fileMode false` (exFAT sets every file to mode 755).
problems.problem: Two issues. (1) The line 68 overlay copies DEV-working-tree/ and DEV-repo-data/, but Capture-RepoData never prunes them, so an edit captured once and later committed (and changed again) stays on the SSD in its old form. `rsync -a` then overwrites the newer clone with it, and git status shows it as uncommitted work. (2) The '755' figure has no source, and CRASHBOX is not mounted, so I could not check it. exFAT has no Unix permission bits, and the core.fileMode step stands either way.
problems.correction: - Copy a `DEV-nonrepo/<folder>` only when GitHub has no repo for it: its copy can hold an older `.git`. The SSD copies are never pruned, so after the overlay run `git -C ~/DEV/<repo> status` and `git checkout -- <file>` for any file the last commit already covers. In each repo that took CRASHBOX files, run `git config core.fileMode false` (exFAT has no Unix permissions, so copied files can arrive marked executable).

problems.line_text: - Each tgz is one copy, replaced on each run, with no history. `codex-memories.tgz` can be old or absent: its source folder no longer exists. Receipts: `Machine/_receipts/run-<id>.txt`. DEV files not on GitHub: copy the folders you need from `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` in the Drive app.
problems.problem: In the live (uncommitted) daily-backup.ps1, the codex-memories.tgz and codex-agents.tgz Snapshot-Gws lines are removed. Any Drive copy of them is frozen at the last upload, and ~/.codex/agents is now backed up only to CRASHBOX codex/agents. ~/.codex/memories is confirmed absent.
problems.correction: - Each tgz is one copy, replaced on each run, with no history. `codex-memories.tgz` and `codex-agents.tgz` are no longer uploaded: skip them; `~/.codex/agents` comes back from CRASHBOX `codex/agents`. Receipts: `Machine/_receipts/run-<id>.txt`. DEV files not on GitHub: copy the folders you need from `_MACHINE/Cloud_Copy/DEV` in the Drive app.

problems.line_text: - Path `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup` (500 GB, exFAT). It gets the second daily copy when plugged in at midday. It is additive: it never deletes.
problems.problem: 'Second daily copy ... at midday' misdescribes the gate in daily-backup-login.sh. The backup runs hourly 12:00-17:00 and at login, on AC power only, at most 2 tries a day, and it stops once a run ends OK. The SSD is written only if it is mounted during that run, and the manifest marks it optional, so an unplugged SSD gives only a warning.
problems.correction: - Path `/Volumes/CRASHBOX/AssistantBackup` (500 GB, exFAT). The daily backup writes to it only if it is mounted when that day's run happens (12:00-17:00 on AC power, or at login); after a run ends OK, no later run that day. It is additive: it never deletes.

problems.problem: Correct for memsearch: the receipt has extras ['onnx'] and config.toml has provider = "onnx". But the second uv tool on the live Mac, cli-anything-hub (which provides ~/.local/bin/cli-hub, used by cli-hub-meta-skill), is never installed.
problems.correction: uv tool install 'memsearch[onnx]' && uv tool install cli-anything-hub && memsearch config set embedding.provider onnx
